---
title: "Project documentation"
---

The raw extension accepts plain numerical arrays and returns plain results.
Optional helpers can make data preparation easier while keeping that boundary
usable directly. These documents are the maintained record of how the project
works and why it makes its choices.

- [Building the documentation](documentation.qmd): Quarto rendering and refreshing computations.
- [Design philosophy](design-philosophy.qmd): priorities, raw interface, helper
  responsibilities and scope.
- [Contracts](contracts.qmd): current PHP and Rust APIs, shapes, ordering, errors
  and statistical edge cases.
- [Development and installation](development.qmd): local setup, separate checkouts,
  builds and application deployment.
- [Verification](verification.qmd): checks, reference fixtures, tolerances and
  evidence limits.
- [Missing data](missing-data.qmd): omission policy, warnings and sample metadata.
- [Walkthrough notebooks](notebooks/index.qmd): executable mathematics and comparisons.
- [OLS verification](verifications/ols.qmd): the same fits in R, statsmodels and PHP.
- [OLS mathematics and Rust notes](ols-math.qmd): derivations and implementation.

Keep the root README as a quick entry point. Put detailed guidance here and
update the relevant document alongside code changes. Distinguish implemented
behavior, verified behavior and proposed direction; do not present plans as
existing features. Add new documents only when a topic needs its own explanation.

The [R compatibility ledger](r-compatibility.qmd) records the expanded weighted,
offset and general Gaussian mixed-model capabilities and remaining work toward
full parity. See the [executed optimizer audit](notebooks/r-compatibility.qmd) and
[random-slopes/REML walkthrough](notebooks/lmm-general-math.qmd).

[Binomial random-intercept models](notebooks/logistic-mixed-math.qmd) now add
non-Gaussian multilevel likelihoods, with
[R/SciPy verification and approximation-error checks](notebooks/logistic-mixed-verification.qmd).
